subject: SDK adaptive batching — field issue during BrightCommerce POC

Cc: James Ortiz <j.ortiz@brightcommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SDK adaptive batching — field issue during BrightCommerce POC

Team,

Quick summary: during this morning's BrightCommerce POC (low QPS demo), the customer saw repeated latency spikes and a few duplicated partial responses when they enabled the SDK's adaptive batching feature (batch_target=auto). They reported the behavior while streaming responses. I captured logs and a tiny reproducer (attached).

Why this matters: BrightCommerce is moving toward a committed Dedicated trial (BR-2381). They've paused the pilot until we confirm whether this is a config/SDK issue or something in the runtime. They want a root-cause and a recommended short-term workaround so they can continue internal demos next week.

What I need from Platform/Runtime + SDK folks:
- Quick triage: known issue? any recent changes to batching or autoscale that could explain duplication + KV/cache behavior?
- Reproducer sanity check: can you reproduce with attached script and logs?
- Short-term workaround we can give the customer (config, SDK flag, model variant).
- ETA for a patch or mitigation plan if it's on our side.

Attachments: bright_bench_reproducer.py, sdk-log-20261127.txt

Thanks — I can hop on a quick sync if helpful.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SDK adaptive batching — field issue during BrightCommerce POC

Thanks for the report, Rachel — good, actionable detail.

Initial triage notes:
- Not a widely reported regression, but we did push an optimization to the batching merge path two weeks ago that changed how small bursts are coalesced. Might be related.
- Need precise SDK version, model name, and whether the customer had prefix/KV caching enabled. The logs look like partial tokens are being retried when a fallback path triggers; that can surface as duplicates in streaming if the KV state isn't properly anchored.

Immediate asks for Bright (cc'ing James):
- SDK version (pip package version or git SHA) and the exact call options used (streaming=true, adaptive_batch=auto, batch_target unspecified?).
- Small reproducer with environment (we have their script attached but will need the command + env vars they used).

Temporary mitigation suggestions (we'll validate):
1) Turn off adaptive batching (adaptive_batch=false) until we confirm.
2) If they need batching, set batch_target to a fixed small integer (e.g., 2) rather than auto.
3) Disable streaming on high-latency flows if duplication is problematic.

I'll try to reproduce locally against a canary runtime. If I can reproduce, I'll open a runtime PR and propose a guard that prevents merging in-flight KV state across autoscale events.

—Dev

Adding a bit of field color from the Bright side (they reproduced on call):
- SDK they used: redwood-sdk 1.6.2 (pip install).
- Model: rwd-compat-large (hosted).
- Call options: streaming=true, adaptive_batch=auto (default), prefetch_kv=true (enabled by default in their client).
- Repro pattern: start a low-rate stream ~0.2 qps for ~30s, then spike to ~8 qps; during the spike they observed 2-3 partial fragments repeated and one complete duplicate in ~1 in 20 responses.
- They ran the attached bright_bench_reproducer.py with --demo-mode and provided sdk-log-20261127.txt (attached).

They asked whether a short config we can hand them will be safe for demos until you have a root-cause.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: James Ortiz <j.ortiz@brightcommerce.com>, Saira Khan <s.khan@brightcommerce.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 08:30:47 -0800
Subject: Re: SDK adaptive batching — field issue during BrightCommerce POC

Update from local repro and initial root cause: I was able to reproduce with the provided script and SDK 1.6.2.

Root cause (summary): a race between the adaptive-batching merge logic and the runtime's transient scaling/fallback path. When the runtime triggers a fallback instance to handle a sudden spike, there is a short window where two partial batches are merged but the KV/prefix anchoring isn't synchronized. That can cause the streaming path to deliver partial token buffers twice for a subset of requests. It's a timing/race issue in the batch-coalescing codepath, not the tokenizer or the model itself.

Planned fix: add an in-flight batch sequence guard so merges respect a per-request KV anchor. I have a patch ready and will open a PR to the runtime repo this morning. Proposed rollout: canary release 2026-11-29T02:00:00Z (UTC) across a small set of hosts, monitor for duplicate-fragment metric. If green, roll to prod in 24–36 hours.

Short-term mitigations for Bright:
- Set adaptive_batch=false (best short-term).
- If they must keep batching: set batch_target=2 and prefetch_kv=false. That combination reproduces reliably for me, so flipping prefetch_kv off avoids the anchor drift.

Docs/attachments: attaching an internal note (adaptive-batching-proposal.pdf) that explains the guard and the test plan.

I'll follow up with the PR link and can assist with a canary for Bright if they want to validate before we roll further.

—Dev
